title: William Gibson and the trademarking of cyberspace
summary: A Hacker News discussion exploring William Gibson, the sci-fi author who coined the term 'cyberspace' in his 1984 novel Neuromancer, and examining the cultural and legal implications of trademarking such influential terminology that has become deeply embedded in our collective vocabulary.
problem_solved: Examines how a single author's coined terminology becomes culturally absorbed and legally contested over time.
why_valuable: Provides valuable insight into the intersection of fiction, technology culture, and intellectual property law by tracing how 'cyberspace' evolved from literary invention to cultural phenomenon.
